title: Leading a WPA band and its personnel
summary: He led one of two WPA bands, with Louis Dumaine leading the other; he lists Charlie Love, Manuel Paul and others.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Charlie Love. Yeah, Charlie Love was playing second trumpet in my band. I was playing first trumpet. See? Then they had a woman who was playing piano. She's a school teacher right now. Her name is Ruby. I forgot her last name. That's all I remember. And Joe Howell was playing sousaphone. And I can't call this guy. This is one of them old Cajuns from down the country was playing banjo. Leo Sanji. Yeah, I don't remember. You don't remember him. Yeah, well, he died. Well, he was playing banjo in the band. He was playing banjo. Joe Howell was playing bass. I was playing fourth trumpet. Charlie Love was playing second trumpet. Manuel Paul was playing tenor saxophone. I forgot who was playing alto. We had another alto horn. I forgot that boy's name. And Ruby was playing the piano. And we used to play at 1420 Canals. We used to start at 8, play from 8 to 11. I'll never forget that. Yeah. I stayed there until the WPA band broke up. That's right. I stayed there. And, uh...
Oh, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. All right.
